title: Why the crusades kept going
question: How did one papal call in 1095 lead to nearly two centuries of campaigns?
hook: One speech in 1095 sent armies east, and each success or failure called for more.
idea: New Crusader states needed defending, so every victory and defeat gave Europe a reason to send another expedition.

beats.prompt: Saladin has united Egypt and Muslim Syria, and the failed Second Crusade has reduced support for crusading in Europe. What happens to the Crusader armies at Hattin in 1187?

choices.label: Fresh European armies arrive and hold the field
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but support for crusading had fallen after the Second Crusade failed.

choices.label: Both sides agree to a truce without a battle
choices.feedback: This is tempting, but the Crusader states were unable to resist Saladin's expansion.

beats.explain: After the Second Crusade failed, the Crusader states could not resist Saladin, who destroyed their combined armies at Hattin.

items: The Mamluks take the last mainland strongholds
beats.explain: The Second Crusade failed in 1148, Hattin followed in 1187, Constantinople was sacked in 1204, and the last mainland strongholds fell in 1291.

beats.prompt: Match each name to what it did.
pairs: Proclaimed the First Crusade at Clermont
Destroyed the Crusader armies at Hattin
Launched the Seventh and Eighth Crusades, which failed
beats.explain: Each of these shaped the course of the Crusades, from the first call to the last mainland losses.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Jerusalem was regained through negotiation during the Sixth Crusade, in 1229.
Soon afterwards, Muslim freebooters sacked Jerusalem and ended Crusader rule in the Holy City.
So Crusader rule in Jerusalem lasted until the Mamluks took the last strongholds in 1291.
So the Crusaders held the Holy City for the rest of the 13th century.
beats.explain: Crusader rule in Jerusalem ended soon after 1229 with its sack by freebooters, long before the Mamluks took the last strongholds in 1291.
